proposals.before: For forty years she never spoke or laughed without cause, and could foretell auspicious days.
proposals.after: For forty years she never spoke or laughed without cause, and never took part in auspicious gatherings.
proposals.reason: 預吉會 means participating in auspicious/festive gatherings, not foretelling days.

proposals.before: For forty years she never spoke or laughed lightly, and could predict auspicious occasions.
proposals.after: For forty years she never spoke or laughed lightly, and never participated in auspicious gatherings.
proposals.reason: 預 means to take part in; predicting is a mistranslation of 預吉會.

proposals.before: Lady Jiao wept and said, "The Yuan family has been unfortunate—three generations of early widowhood. From my husband's great-grandmother onward all have kept their chastity. How can I be the one to break it!
proposals.after: Lady Jiao wept and said, "The Yuan family has been unfortunate—three generations of early widowhood. From my husband's grandmother onward all have kept their chastity. How can I be the one to break it!
proposals.reason: 祖姑 here aligns with 祖母 (grandmother-in-law) in the three-generation widow sequence, not a great-grandmother.

proposals.before: There was also the Wu family of Xinghe, who pricked her own face;
proposals.after: There was also Lady Wu of Xinghe, who pricked her own face;
proposals.reason: 吳氏 with feminine 自刺 denotes an individual woman, not a family.

proposals.before: There was also the Wu clan of Xinghe, who pricked her own face;
proposals.after: There was also Lady Wu of Xinghe, who pricked her own face;
proposals.reason: 吳氏 is an individual widow in the exemplary-woman formula, not a clan.

proposals.before: Widowed young, her parents had her remarry; she would not comply.
proposals.after: Widowed young, her parents urged her to remarry, but she would not comply.
proposals.reason: 使再醮，不從 means they sought to make her remarry and she refused; 'had her remarry' wrongly implies the remarriage occurred.

proposals.before: The Feng clan, named Shuan, style Jingjun, was a daughter of a great-name official family and the second wife of Li Ruzhong, magistrate of Shanyin county in Shandong.
proposals.after: Feng, named Shuan, style Jingjun, was a daughter of a Daming official family and the second wife of Li Ruzhong, magistrate of Shanyin county in Shandong.
proposals.reason: 馮氏，名淑安 is an individual; 'Feng clan' and 'great-name' misread 氏 and 大名.

proposals.before: Ruzhong had first married a Mongol woman and borne a son named Ren, who died at a few years of age.
proposals.after: Ruzhong had first married a Mongol woman and they had a son named Ren; after a few years she died.
proposals.reason: Later narrative takes living Ren away and leaves the Mongol woman's coffin; 卒 refers to the wife.

proposals.before: Ruzhong first married a Mongol woman and bore a son named Ren, who died at several years of age.
proposals.after: Ruzhong first married a Mongol woman and they had a son named Ren; after several years she died.
proposals.reason: Consistency with 子任 taken away and 蒙古氏之柩 shows the wife died, not the son.

proposals.before: The crowd prepared her body. She was buried in linked coffins with her husband. More than three hundred people escorted them, and none failed to weep.
proposals.after: The crowd prepared her body. She was buried in linked coffins with her husband. Several hundred people escorted them, and none failed to weep.
proposals.reason: 數百人 means several hundred, not a count above three hundred.

proposals.before: The Yelü clan was the wife of Yelü Hudubuhua, assistant administrator of Huzhou circuit.
proposals.after: Lady Yila was the wife of Yelü Hudubuhua, assistant administrator of Huzhou circuit.
proposals.reason: 移剌氏 is an individual wife, not a clan predicated as 'was the wife'.

proposals.before: At sixteen Maimu was posted to Qiantang as an official and died of illness. He was buried ten li west of the city.
proposals.after: When she was sixteen, Maimu, posted to Qiantang as an official, died of illness. He was buried ten li west of the city.
proposals.reason: 年十六 marks the widow Wang's age at her husband's death in this biography, not Maimu's age.

proposals.before: At sixteen Maimu served as an official at Qiantang and died of illness; he was buried ten li west of the city.
proposals.after: At sixteen, Maimu, serving as an official at Qiantang, died of illness; he was buried ten li west of the city.
proposals.reason: Same age-referent error: 年十六 is Wang's age in context.

proposals.before: The righteous wife Zhang was from Zouping in Jinan, eighteen years old when she returned home and married Li Wu of her village.
proposals.after: The righteous wife Zhang was from Zouping in Jinan; at eighteen she married Li Wu of her village.
proposals.reason: 歸 is the marriage verb for a woman here, not a literal return home.

proposals.before: The officials praised her righteousness and reported to the great prefecture. Ling was sent to escort the coffin home, money was given for burial, an honorific gate was erected, and corvée was restored as prescribed.
proposals.after: The officials praised her righteousness and reported to the great prefecture. Ling was sent to escort the coffin home, money was given for burial, an honorific gate was erected, and their corvée was remitted.
proposals.reason: 復其役 remits or exempts corvée service rather than restoring labor obligations.

proposals.before: The officials praised her righteousness and reported upward to the great prefecture; they had Ling escort the coffin back, gave money for burial, still erected an honorific gate, and restored corvée as prescribed.
proposals.after: The officials praised her righteousness and reported upward to the great prefecture; they had Ling escort the coffin back, gave money for burial, still erected an honorific gate, and remitted their corvée.
proposals.reason: Same 復其役 misreading as restoring rather than remitting corvée.

proposals.before: The Bai clan was from Taiyuan.
proposals.after: Bai was from Taiyuan.
proposals.reason: 白氏 here names the exemplary woman, not the Bai clan as a collective.

proposals.before: The Bai clan was from Taiyuan.
proposals.after: Bai was from Taiyuan.
proposals.reason: Same error: 白氏 is the woman's designation, not a clan collective.

proposals.before: Lady Li was the wife of Huo Gao'er of Binzhou.
proposals.after: Lady Li was the wife of Hui Gao'er of Binzhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 惠高兒 is Hui Gao'er; Huo misreads 惠 as 霍.

proposals.before: The Li clan was the wife of Huo Gao'er of Binzhou.
proposals.after: Lady Li was the wife of Hui Gao'er of Binzhou.
proposals.reason: 李氏 denotes Lady Li, not a clan as subject; 惠 is Hui not Huo.

proposals.before: During the Zhiding era Quan died of illness. Zhizhen grieved, wept, refused food, and died after several days.
proposals.after: During the Taiding era Quan died of illness. Zhizhen grieved, wept, refused food, and died after several days.
proposals.reason: 泰定 is Taiding, not Zhiding.

proposals.before: During the Zhiding era Quan died of illness; Zhizhen grieved and wept without eating and died after several days.
proposals.after: During the Taiding era Quan died of illness; Zhizhen grieved and wept without eating and died after several days.
proposals.reason: 泰定 is Taiding, not Zhiding.

decisions.reason: In s0023 四十年未嘗妄言笑，預吉會, 預 means take part in and 吉會 are auspicious/festive gatherings; 未嘗 scopes over the parallel phrase, so she never joined such gatherings—not that she could foretell days.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 四十年未嘗妄言笑，預吉會

decisions.reason: Literal s0023 likewise misreads 預吉會 as predicting occasions; 預 is participate, and with carried 未嘗 the clause denies participation in auspicious gatherings.
s0078 自祖姑以來 names the husband's grandmother (祖姑), matching s0076 祖母楊氏 in the three-generation widow sequence; great-grandmother would be 曾祖姑.
s0128 興和吳氏，自刺其面 uses the exemplary-woman 氏 formula for one widow who pricked her own face, parallel to the named wives in s0129–s0130—not a family collective.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 又有興和吳氏，自刺其面

decisions.reason: Literal 吳氏 is likewise an individual; 'Wu clan' wrongly collective-izes the subject of feminine 自刺其面.
s0149 父母使再醮，不從 is attempt plus refusal; 'had her remarry' wrongly implies the remarriage was carried out despite 不從.
s0158 馮氏，名淑安 identifies an individual woman, and 大名 is the place Daming, not the adjective 'great-name'.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 馮氏，名淑安，字靜君，大名宦家女

decisions.reason: Though 生子任，數歲而卒 is locally ambiguous, later s0164 removes living 子任 and s0165 leaves 蒙古氏之柩, so 卒 is the Mongol wife's death, not the son's.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 初娶蒙古氏，生子任，數歲而卒

decisions.reason: Same referent: s0164–s0165 show Ren taken away alive and the Mongol wife's coffin remaining, so literal 卒 must mark her death.
s0177 送者數百人 means several hundred escorts, not a figure above three hundred.
s0178 移剌氏…妻也 predicates an individual wife (移剌/Yila), not a clan as the grammatical wife of Yelü Hudubuhua.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 移剌氏，同知湖州路事耶律忽都不花妻也

decisions.reason: After s0200 names Wang as subject, s0201 年十六 marks her age when 買奴官錢塘病歿; the original wrongly makes sixteen Maimu's age.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 年十六，買奴官錢塘病歿

decisions.after: When she was sixteen, Maimu, serving as an official at Qiantang, died of illness; he was buried ten li west of the city.
decisions.reason: 年十六 is Wang's age, but the proposed literal still opens with 'At sixteen, Maimu…,' which keeps Maimu as the age referent; make the widow the explicit subject of the age phrase.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 年十六，買奴官錢塘病歿

decisions.reason: In s0211 年十八歸里人李伍, 歸 is the standard verb for a woman marrying, not a literal return home before marriage.
In reward formulae 復其役 remits/exempts corvée (cf. s0127 复役如製); 'restored' reverses the privilege.
Literal 復其役 is the same exemption privilege, not restoration of labor duty.
s0240 白氏，太原人 introduces the individual exemplary woman continued as 白氏 in s0242, not the Bai clan as a collective.
Literal likewise: 白氏 is her designation, not a clan subject.
s0254 惠高兒 is Hui Gao'er; Huo misreads 惠 as 霍.
李氏 is Lady Li as individual wife, and 惠高兒 is Hui not Huo; 'Li clan' plus Huo are both wrong.
s0298 泰定間 is the Taiding era (1324–1328), not Zhiding.
Literal same error: 泰定 is Taiding, not Zhiding.
